README.mdApplication guide

About the model

ADE Simulator is a C++ application for modelling advection, dispersion, and adsorption–desorption in a porous medium. It includes equilibrium and kinetic sorption, with controls for transport, reactions, and spatial and temporal discretization.

The desktop and browser applications use the same ImGui interface and shared solver code. Browser-specific adapters handle files, rendering, and background computation.

Research software

Review model assumptions, convergence, and mass balance for your own application. Numerical regression tests do not establish scientific validity for every scenario.

Getting started

  1. Choose a version. Install the Windows application or open the browser app using the links above.
  2. Create or open a project. Choose a saved project from the startup list, create one, or import an existing INI file. Set model inputs in the Config panel.
  3. Run the simulation. Select the Run button in the title bar. Transport plots update while the calculation runs; use Stop to cancel.
  4. Inspect the results. Open Log for messages and Info for model diagnostics. Use File → Save Project to keep your parameters, observations, and results.

One familiar workspace

Config
Set discretization, transport, and reaction parameters.
Graph
Inspect transport, calibration, sensitivity, and uncertainty views.
Log & Info
Read execution messages and inspect numerical diagnostics.

The browser version keeps docked panels within the browser canvas. Use a desktop-sized screen for the full configuration workspace.

Working with files

Use INI files for model parameters and CSV files for observation data and exported results. In the browser, file pickers import into temporary storage.

After saving results, select File → Download exported files to transfer them to your computer. Download anything you want to keep before refreshing or closing the page.

Saved projects are local to this device and browser. Use File → Save Project before closing; clearing site data removes saved projects. Use File → Projects / New Project to save or discard changes before switching.

The web app needs a modern browser with WebGL, WebAssembly threads, and service workers enabled. Its first visit may reload once to prepare browser support.
